bodies: We test what affects your plumbing and your taste, like hardness, chlorine and sediment, and explain the results plainly.

Chicago's Lake Michigan water is treated and tested by the city. The pipes inside a century-old home are a separate question. For health-related testing, a state-certified lab can run a full panel, and we'll point you to one.

blocks.intro: The city treats the water. What happens inside an older home depends on its pipes.

items.body: Old galvanized pipe can affect taste, color and pressure.
A whole-house filter treats everything. An under-sink filter treats drinking water.
Filtration helps keep new faucets and appliances clean.

blocks.h2: What Happens When You Call J. Blanton

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber in shoe covers on a home's front steps with a sewer camera

blocks.body: Chicago treats and tests its Lake Michigan water before it reaches your street. Inside an older Ravenswood home, the water then passes through decades-old pipe and fixtures. A filter at the kitchen sink is the simplest way to improve drinking water. A whole-house filter treats everything. If you're seeing rusty water or low pressure, the pipe itself may need attention, and we'll tell you if a filter is masking a bigger problem.

blocks.h2: Water Filtration Questions From Ravenswood Homeowners

items.q: Do I need a whole-house filter or an under-sink filter?
items.answer: For better drinking water, an under-sink or reverse osmosis filter is enough. For filtered water at every tap and shower, a whole-house system.

items.preview: It's treated. Filters are for taste and peace of mind.
items.answer: Chicago's water is treated and tested. Many people filter for taste or peace of mind, especially in older homes.

items.q: I saw 'well water filtration' online. Does that apply here?
items.preview: No. Ravenswood is on city water.
items.answer: No. Homes in Ravenswood are on Chicago city water, not wells. City water filters are what fit here.

items.q: How often do filters need changing?
items.answer: Under-sink cartridges every several months. Whole-house filters vary.

items.q: Does a filter replace old pipes?
items.answer: No. A filter improves the water you drink. Failing pipe still needs repair.

items.q: How much does water filtration cost in Ravenswood?
items.preview: It depends on the system. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the system and installation. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we install.
